text.p: Belgian brokerage KB Securities sees shares in Belgian data and telecommunications group Telinfo increasing by five to 10 percent in the near term.
Analyst Johan Pede (+32 2 546 41 61) expects Telinfo to realise EPS growth of 20 to 25 percent in the next three years due to high demand for networking services.
From 1998 onwards the company should benefit from accelerating telecoms deregulation in Europe, fast growing needs for additional, Internet-related, capacity and a better EU investment climate.
Investment conclusions:
Planned acquisitions -- priority is given to France and Spain -- will offer important economies of scale.
Together with France Telecom, Telinfo will soon bid for new GSM-licenses in Luxembourg and Holland.
Telinfo's 10 percent stake in Belgian GSM mobile telephone network Mobistar is valued at 2.9 billion Belgian francs. Mobistar is expected to not contribute to earnings before 2000.

Adjusted for the value of Mobistar the stock (at 2,160 francs) is trading at a P/E for 1997 of 32, more or less in line with growth stocks such as Barco and competitors such as Simac and Getronics of the Netherlands.
Outlook:

The stake in Mobistar is a major pearl. Its penetration now amounts to about 1.7 percent compared to about 4.6 percent for Belgacom's Proximus. Telinfo expects total indirect revenues from Mobistar in 1996-2000 of one billion francs.
In 1997 the group will benefit from large projects such as Isabel, the Belgian electronic banking platform.
In the longer term Telinfo will benefit from an expected recovery in the European investment climate from 1998 onwards.
KB Securities expects the tax rate to increase gradually to 26 percent in 1999 as profit from new and foreign entities becomes more significant.
Acquisitions in the coming months and years in telecoms services will give Telinfo the critical mass to become a top-three player in large European markets.
Estimates: (Belgian francs, source KB Securities, July 3)
Earnings/share 41 50 62 76
Gross dividend 8 10 12 15
